title: Coloring A Border
summary: Given an m x n grid where each cell is colored with a specific color, and a target cell's coordinates, you are to change the color of the bordering cells of the target cell's connected component to a specified color.
statement: Given an m x n grid where each cell is colored with a specific color, and a target cell's coordinates, you are to change the color of the bordering cells of the target cell's connected component to a specified color. Cells are considered adjacent if they are next to each other either horizontally or vertically. The border of a connected component consists of cells that are either adjacent to cells not in the component or are on the edge of the grid. Return the modified grid after coloring the border.
constraints: Recolor only component cells on the grid edge or adjacent to a different color.
hints: First discover the component without changing colors that connectivity checks rely on.
A component cell is border when on an edge or beside a noncomponent cell.
DFS/BFS records border coordinates, then recolor those coordinates afterward.
Discovery visits exactly the component and the local border predicate matches the definition.
